headline: Two US senators from opposite parties have proposed a bill to make the makers and operators of AI agents legally liable when their agents hack computer systems.
score_reason: Verified and new; a bill only, so no change to the pool score.
importance_line: It would make AI companies and their executives answerable, up to prison time under Murphy's description, for harm from agents that hack, but it has only been announced and the White House opposes new AI rules.
summary: MeriTalk reports that Republican Josh Hawley and Democrat Chris Murphy announced the AI Agent Accountability Act, which would apply the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act, the main US anti-hacking law, to operators who knowingly run an agent that recklessly causes hacking damage, and would make developers criminally and civilly liable if they failed to put in reasonable safeguards after they knew or had reason to know of an agent's hacking ability. It is only a proposal, and MeriTalk notes that President Trump has repeatedly rejected extra AI regulation.
